text: Import a spec-driven tasks.md (GitHub spec-kit, spec-workflow-mcp) into the idea graph
description: Major hypothesis loop 2026-11-02. RESEARCHED: spec-driven development is where coding-agent users already plan: spec-workflow-mcp (4.1k stars, https://gittrend.io/repo/Pimzino/spec-workflow-mcp), GitHub spec-kit, Claude Code plugins like Tasker (https://skillselion.com/plugin/Dowwie/tasker); their output is requirements.md / design.md / tasks.md. INFERRED: those files are flat checklists per feature with no value flow, no cross-session priority and no hypotheses, which is what Aimparency adds. Smallest experiment: an import (like import_github_issues) that turns a spec folder's tasks.md into a parent idea per spec with one child per task (checked = implemented), tested on spec-kit's own example spec. Stop if the formats differ too much to map without guessing.

status.comment: MCP tool import_spec_tasks (packages/mcp/src/tools/repos.ts) -> backend idea.importSpecTasks + pure parser packages/backend/src/spec-tasks.ts. Finds every tasks.md at or below a path inside the repo (refuses paths outside), one parent 'Spec tasks: <spec folder>' per file, one child per top-level checklist item, [x] implemented / [-] partially, indented lines as description, marker 'Spec task <file>#<id>'. Re-runs add new tasks and move ideas of tasks ticked since forward (open -> partially -> implemented), never back, so the graph can be ahead of the file. Checked against the real templates: spec-kit '- [ ] T001 ...' under '## Phase' headings, spec-workflow-mcp '- [ ] 4.1 ...' with indented details. Verified: spec-tasks.test.ts 4/4 (both formats, re-import adds only the new task, ticked task advances while an unticked one stays implemented, path guard), backend + mcp tsc clean, mcp tests 54/54. README mentions it next to the GitHub import. Adoption hypothesis on the parent edge stays untested until outside users see it.
